samples.summary: `prompt` slice is unbounded to EOF, so the ordering assertions can be satisfied by text belonging to other jobs
samples.evidence: The test builds `prompt = wf.slice(wf.indexOf("The review panel requested changes on your PR."))` with no end bound, so it covers the rest of agent-review-panel.yml (the `fix` job ends at line 1915 but `close-stuck-checks` and `stalled` follow). `push = prompt.indexOf("Push with `git push --no-verify`")` and the `/BEFORE PUSHING/`, `/PUSH LAST/` matches therefore aren't scoped to the fixer prompt: if the fixer's push paragraph were deleted or reworded and any later job's prompt gained an equivalent line, `report < push` and the prose assertions would still pass while the guarded property (ordering inside the fixer prompt) had been lost. Bounding the slice at the end of the `fix` job's prompt block would make the test fail for the right reason.

samples.summary: The new "AFTER COMMITTING" half of the changed instruction is not asserted anywhere
samples.evidence: The prompt edit introduces a three-step ordering — commit, then report, then push ("REPORT WHAT YOU DID — AFTER COMMITTING, BEFORE PUSHING", workflow line 1665). The test asserts only the report-before-push half (`report < push`, plus `/BEFORE PUSHING/` and `/PUSH LAST/`). Nothing asserts the commit-before-report requirement, so a future edit that drops "AFTER COMMITTING" (leaving the fixer free to report before committing, which makes the report describe uncommitted work) passes the suite. Searched fix-report.test.mjs for /AFTER COMMITTING|commit/ assertions and grepped scripts/agent/*.test.mjs for other workflow-prompt tests; only this test reads the workflow file for ordering.
